text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Haris Silajdzic, co-chairman for the Bosnian Council of Ministers, deplores police intervention against protesters in Belgrade and says: "Abuse of force against citizens has to be a thing of the past. Human rights and democracy are the future".
- A 70-year old Moslem woman has disappeared from Croat- controlled western Mostar. Police investigation indicated that her flat has been seized.
- The World Bank pledged three more funds for reconstruction projects in Bosnia, including $17 million for development of small private companies and $15 million for the reconstruction of hospitals.

- Self-styled Bosnian Croat state Herceg Bosnia disbanded a few weeks ago will probably remain as an underground state or as a "national Croat community" which will be disappearing or appearing according to its political needs, Sarajevo's daily Dnevni Avaz writes.
